sources.entry: Control Group v2 - Defines cpu.max throttling, cpu.weight and the cpusets that bound affinity, the controls behind every container limit.

summary.title: Control Group v2
summary.one_liner: Learn how cgroup v2 organizes processes into a single hierarchy, how controllers are enabled and delegated, and how weight- and limit-based resource distribution works.
keywords: how do containers limit cpu linux
takeaways: cgroup v2 uses a single unified hierarchy, mounted with mount -t cgroup2, and every process belongs to exactly one cgroup.
Controllers such as cpu and memory are enabled per cgroup via cgroup.subtree_control, and only distribute resources to child cgroups.
The no internal process constraint means domain controllers need processes to live only in leaf cgroups.
Delegation lets less privileged users manage sub-hierarchies, with containment enforced on process migration.
Threaded mode lets threads of a process spread across a subtree, with cpu, cpuset, perf_event and pids as threaded controllers.
summary.summary: This is the kernel's authoritative documentation for control group v2, written by Tejun Heo in 2015. It covers the core concepts of cgroups as a hierarchy of processes, the mounting and mount options, and how processes and threads are organized and migrated. It then explains how controllers are enabled and disabled, the top-down constraint, the no internal process constraint, and delegation rules. The page ends by introducing resource distribution models such as weight-based distribution; the excerpt cuts off in that section.
